title: Use raw Classroom assignments as chat candidates (no task splitting)
description:
## Context
Chat candidates are currently plan items (already split into smaller steps). We want the coach to reason over *raw* Classroom assignments instead, and only generate/suggest a next step after the user has chosen (or the coach has recommended) an assignment.

## Scope
Includes:
- Define the *candidate schema* for raw Classroom assignments (fields + limits)
- Define the *selection contract* (what ID is selected and where it is stored)
- Update backend chat candidate construction to use raw assignments
- Update coach prompts to match the new contract
- Update/extend tests to reflect the new contract

Excludes (explicit non-goals for this epic):
- Redesigning weekly planning / planner logic end-to-end
- Building a full new UI flow in iOS (beyond what is strictly required by API contract)
- Changing Google Classroom import behavior (separate epic)

## Key Decisions (must be explicit)
- Selection ID: do we keep `selected_plan_item_id` but point it at assignment IDs, or introduce a new field like `selected_assignment_id`?
- Post-selection behavior: after an assignment is selected, do we (a) ask one clarifying question, (b) suggest a 30–120s first step, or (c) run just-in-time task-splitting for that one assignment?

## Deliverables
- Written contract: candidate schema + selection rules + example behaviors
- Backend sends candidates as raw assignments in `/chat/send` debug traces
- Prompts updated to treat candidates as the source of truth and avoid hallucinating details

## Success Criteria
- `/chat/send` candidates are raw Classroom assignments (no breakdown) and include sufficient fields for grounding
- The coach reliably selects a relevant assignment when the user expresses a preference (measured via evals)
- No increase in invented details (measured via evals + spot-checking traces)

## Dependencies / Assumptions
- Assumes we will have an eval harness (see eval epic) to measure selection + hallucination regressions.

## Risks / Notes
- Prompt contract drift can break selection (IDs) silently; keep a single source of truth for the schema and add tests.
- Longer descriptions/attachments can bloat prompts; schema must include truncation rules.

title: Deployment infrastructure for Study Buddy backend
description:
## Context
We need a repeatable way to deploy the backend with proper config/secrets and basic observability.

## Scope
Includes:
- Hosting target selection + environment setup
- Build/run packaging (container or equivalent)
- Secrets management + configuration
- Basic logs/health checks
Excludes:
- Scaling/multi-region

## Success Criteria
- Backend deploys from main to a stable environment
- Config/secrets are not committed; managed via platform secrets
- Health endpoint + smoke test succeeds post-deploy
- Minimal logging/monitoring is in place

title: Eval repo + process for Study Buddy coaching
description:
## Context
We need a repeatable way to measure coaching quality and prevent regressions when we change prompts/candidate inputs.

## Scope
Includes:
- Golden test set (anonymized)
- Eval runner + report
- CI integration (PR gate)
Excludes:
- Deployment / hosting

## Success Criteria
- One command produces a scored report (pass/fail + summary)
- PRs run evals automatically and fail on regressions beyond an agreed threshold
- Dataset + eval artifacts are stored in a repo-friendly way (versioned)

## Risks / Notes
- Must avoid leaking student data; require anonymization/redaction

title: Define eval rubric + scoring metrics
description:
## Acceptance Criteria
- Metrics are defined (selection correctness, hallucination, language, thread coherence)
- Scoring thresholds and pass/fail policy are documented
- 10 example cases with expected outcomes are produced

title: Define golden dataset format + redaction/anonymization rules
description:
## Acceptance Criteria
- JSON schema for eval cases is defined
- Redaction/anonymization rules are documented
- 30+ cases exist in the agreed location

title: Implement eval runner + report output
description:
## Acceptance Criteria
- One command runs all cases and outputs a machine-readable report + human summary
- Report includes per-case failures with enough debug context to fix
- Baseline run is saved for comparison
